Commentary.Commentary: Taking into account the way the wicket is playing, plus the fact that the hosts have three quality spinners in their ranks, the Proteas have a difficult task ahead of them, to say the least. Their inability to bowl out Sri Lanka towards the end of Day 1 could seriously come back to haunt them. They're going to have to play out of their skins now. The second innings will start shortly, don't go anywhere...

On Day 1, Sri Lanka started the day well with a good opening stand, but then had their momentum halted by Keshav Maharaj in the afternoon session, only to be revived again by Dhananjaya de Silva and Roshen Silva. Though, Maharaj had his say again and took 8 wickets in total at the end of the day, toppling the Lankan batsmen with ease. He scalped the last wicket today as well.

So, finally, South Africa managed to take the final wicket of the Lankan innings, but it's probably come a little too late. They allowed the last pair to add 74 runs together, thereby allowing Sri Lanka to get close to 340, a score which is gargantuan on this turning surface. It was expected that the tourists would clean things up rather early this morning, but Rangana Herath and Akila Dananjaya played some attacking cricket and put their side in a strong position.

OUT! The decision stands! Keshav Maharaj finishes with career-best figures in Test cricket. Tossed up on leg, Herath is down to sweep but gets it off the glove, then the pad and it pops up behind to Elgar at leg slip who takes a regulation catch. The finger goes up, but the batsman reviews it. The TV umpire comes into the pitcure and replays show Herath is gone. So, SRI LANKA ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 338!
Review taken. Rangana Herath has been caught at leg slip and given out, but the review has been taken, probably because it's the last wicket and it's not going to harm anyone.
Short ball banged in, ducked and evaded.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Another pull on the leg side. One more to the total.
Short ball which doesn't rise as much, Dananjaya swivels to pull but gets it off the glove through square leg for one.
Length delivery attacking the stumps, Akila close the bat face slightly and blocks it towards mid-wicket.
Short of a length delivery on off, Herath rises on his toes and dabs it behind point for a single.
Drinks break.
Back to over the wicket and it's bowled full outside off, Dananjaya prods forward and solidly keeps it out.
Offers a straight bat in defense to this straighter one.
Drags his length back just a bit, this time the batsman stays inside the crease and defends.
Spinning on off stump, another solid front foot defense in response.
From around the wicket now, it's looped up on the stumps, Akila is forward in defense.
FOUR! Short and turning in from outside off, Dananjaya rocks onto his back foot in a flash and cuts it behind point fiercely. No stopping that, a boundary results.
Bumper once again. Herath ignores it for the keeper.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.

FOUR! BANG! Highest 10th wicket stand against South Africa for Sri Lanka. This is Herath or Sangakkara? It's hard to differentiate right now. He is playing Steyn like a top-order batsman and thrashing him everywhere. A length ball lofted over mid on and it races into the boundary.
And short again from Dale. Akila pulls it through mid-wicket for another single. It's all too easy for the Lankans right now.
Another short ball, pulled through square leg this time. One run taken.
FOUR! Slapped! Welcome the crease Mr. Steyn. Herath is in no mood get bullied. He pulls across the back of a length ball and gets it in the gap through mid-wicket. A boundary results.
A length ball outside off, driven through covers by Akila. They take two from the deep.
Fuller on off, pushed to covers for a quick single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Action replay from the bowler and the batsman.
Flatter in line of the stumps, played to the on side.
Gets behind the line to this one and keeps it out.
Square cuts the length ball to end the over.
A touch short around off, played through point for a run.
Full toss on leg, swept through the on side. One run taken.
The batsman has driven that ball straight back.
Fuller on off, lofted over Rabada at long off by Herath. He manages to save a run for his team.
Slow on off, cut to covers.
Loopy in line of the stumps, turning into the batsman, Herath goes deep inside the crease before working it away on the leg side.
Positions himself perfectly behind the line and blocks.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Bit fullish in length and on the stumps, blocked from within the crease.
Floated around off, this one doesn't turn, Herath is forward is defense and gets beaten past the outside edge.
FOUR BYES! Tossed up on leg and spinning down, Herath looks to defend but it misses everything and goes fine down the leg side past the keeper. It runs away to the fence for a boundary.
Again shorter outside off, cut through backward point for a brace.
A tad shorter, blocked off the back foot by Akila.
Reverse sweeps it out. Herath is putting all his arsenal on display here. A flighted ball around off, Herath changes hands and gets it off his gloves behind the keeper. One run taken.
Ngidi is off unfortunately. Markram bowls a good flatter delivery on off, Herath gets behind the line and defends it.

There seems to be some problem with Lungi Ngidi. He got hit on his left ankle and looks in some pain. The physio is in the middle to check on him. Off he goes, SA not risking their premier fast bowler. Aiden Markram will finish the over for him.
On the pads, flicked to the on side for a run.

Ouch! He is down flat on his stomach. Dananjaya connected with the length ball well and hits it straight on Ngidi's left ankle. It looked as if he got hand to it but not really. He looks in pain while going back to his bowling mark.

He survives! Herath, you lucky, lucky man. Had the ball not kissed the glove on the way to the pads, he would have been a goner. Intelligent from Maharaj, he keeps it in the same channel. Herath looks to play across the line this time but misses. The bowler is confident and he convinces his skipper to take the review who follows his advice. Perhaps not the right decision as the replays shows that the ball kissed the glove and that saved him. South Africa have lost both their reviews now.
The review for the LBW has been taken by Faf. Rangana Herath is the man in question. He looks out.
Maharaj goes over the wicket and bowls a tossed up delivery around middle. Rangana looks to defend it but misses. An appeal ensues but the umpire ignores it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A touch faster in the same line, easily tackled by Rangana.
Similar delivery from Maharaj. Herath happy to block it.
Flighted outside off, defended off the front foot.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Short in line of the stumps, played off the back foot for nothing.
Flicked aerially through square leg. One run taken. Herath is looking set for a long innings.
FOUR! He is making the bowlers pay for the average bowling. A length ball from Ngidi outside off, Herath punches it from his crease and gets it through cover-point for a boundary.
Again going across the left-hander and it goes down the leg side. Herath misses it this time.
Wide down the leg side, the batsman leaves it alone.
Lungi Ngidi is on.
Hangs back and dishes it off the front foot.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, guided to third man for a run by Rangana.
Tossed up outside off, Herath goes near the ball and defends it again.
Gets behind the line of this one and defends it.
Faster and flatter targeting the sticks, Herath lunges forward and gets an edge but luckily for him, it goes left of Bavuma. He survives again.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! 300 it is. Sri Lanka cross the mark for the first time in the series and worries for South Africa. A full ball outside off, Dananjaya throws his bat at it and gets it off the outer half of the blade through point.
Nicely tackled by Akila. A short ball in line of the stumps, Dananjaya hops and keeps it out.
Bouncer! Akila ducks in time to let that one go over him.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball but fails.
Chips the shortish delivery to the on side and changes strike.
Hangs back and sees out the last ball of the over. Sri Lanka inching closer to the 300-run mark.
Works this one to the on side off the back foot.
FOUR! Edgy but effective. Dananjaya goes for the cut to the ball spinning in from a length. He only manages to get it from the outside half of his bat and the ball races to the third man fence.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Flatter on middle and off this time, defended off the front foot.
Again comes down the track but only connects with thin air, as he gets hits on the pads again.
Uppish but safe. A length ball on middle and off, Herath pushes at it from his crease and gets it past the bowler.
Herath closes the face of the bat early and gets a leading edge on that one. No harm done.
Well played. Another length ball on off, Herath has a swipe against the line and manages to get it through mid-wicket. A brace results.
Defended off the back foot by Rangana. This one stayed a touch low but nicely tackled by the veteran.
Short and across Herath who does well to leave it for the keeper.
Rabada goes around the wicket and bowls a yorker on middle and off, Herath does well to dig it out.
That ball has struck Dananjaya on the thigh pad. A flighted ball outside off, it spins in and evades the bat of Akila. No harm done in the end.
Comes charging down the track and plays it towards mid-wicket. He is trying different things to play Maharaj it seems.
Flatter on off, pushed down the track for no run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Easy peasy. Experience coming into play here. Herath dabs it to the covers and runs a quick single.
Flighted around off, played off the front foot by Herath.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Around off, played to the off side.

So cool this little man. A short of a length ball targeting the rib cage of Herath, he swivels and pulls it to fine leg for a single. Though one hand was off the handle but he still managed to play it well.
A wild slog across the line this time from Herath. He misses it.
FOUR! Herath slashes at it and earns a boundary. A full ball outside off, he throws his bat at it and manages to get it over backward point.
Herath has done well to keep that yorker at bay.
Pushed to the on side this time. Dananjaya is playing Maharaj relatively well.
Faster this time, Dananjaya looks to poke at it and misses again.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Shortish on leg, played down on the leg side for nothing.
Hangs back and defends it down the track.
Comes down the track but misses the ball to get hit on the pads.
Short ball towards the ribs, just goes past Bavuma at short leg. One run results.
Wide down the leg side, the batsman leaves it alone.
FOUR! Cheeky from Dananjaya. A short ball from Rabada, Akila plays the ramp shot and gets it up and over the slip cordon. A boundary!
In line of the stumps, blocked off from his crease by Akila.
Outside off, Dananjaya misses the cut.
Rabada starts with a back of a length ball around off, Herath gets it away off the back foot and takes a run. First run of the morning for Sri Lanka.
Kagiso Rabada to bowl from the other end.
Akila survives the first over from Maharaj. He gets forward and blocks it out.
Ooh! Just manages to evade the short leg fielder. Maharaj is testing Akila straightaway.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Slower on off, it spins in and hits Dananjaya on his pad.
Similar delivery from Maharaj, played just away from short leg.
Starts with a dangerous ball around middle and leg. Gives it air and draws Dananjaya forward who defends it off the inner half of the bat to the on side.
We are set for the action to start. The players are out in the middle. Akila Dananjaya will take the strike and Keshav Maharaj has the newish ball in his hand. Here we go...

Pitch report - Shaun Pollock along with Kepler Wessels is reporting from the pitch and says that there are rough areas on the good length area. Wessels asserts this is a track that will have fast and vicious spin. They further add that the left-handers will be troubled more by the patches on the middle of the surface and the three Lankan spinners will be really looking forward to bowl against the visiting batsmen.

Hello! Welcome to the second day of the second and final Test match between Sri Lanka and South Africa at Sinhalese Sports Club, Colombo. Both the teams will be partially happy and partially sad after the action on Day 1 as both of them have an almost equal foothold in the game as of now. The home team has ended the first day on 277 on a pitch which started spitting venom in the very first hour of play. Considering the visitors could only score 199 in both the innings combined in the last Test, the Lankans will be hoping to get to the psychological total of 300 and finish off their challenge with the bat later on. The African team's target is to dismiss Sri Lanka's remaining lone wicket and play for as long as possible. The action starts in a while, stay tuned!
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

That's all from Day 1. The visitors will look to get the last wicket as soon as possible but they will have to bat really well to get into the game. The pitch is turning prodigiously and Sri Lanka have three quality spinners in their ranks as well. Do join us for all the action from Day 2 at 1000 local (0430 GMT). For now, you can switch tabs to catch the Zimbabwe-Pakistan match. Till then, cheers!

Earlier in the day, Sri Lanka started on a positive note. Their openers stitched a 116-run stand and gave them the upper hand. However, they lost their way post Lunch with a couple of wickets. Dhananjaya de Silva along with Roshen Silva added 54 for the 5th wicket to get them back on track. The former then stroked his way to his 3rd Test fifty, however, there were no real contributions from the lower middle order. Akila Dananjaya is still in the middle with Rangana Herath and the hosts will hope he gets quick runs on Day 2 to extend the Proteas' worries.

South Africa will be happy with the day's result after the start the home team had. They have one man to thank - Keshav Maharaj. The left-arm orthodox spinner took 8/116, which is the best for any visiting spinner in Sri Lanka and helped restrict Sri Lanka to 277/9. Perhaps now Faf du Plessis will regret the decision of not playing the second spinner. Kagiso Rabada got the other lone wicket, but had there been Tabraiz Shamsi in the playing XI, this would paint another picture.
Length ball around off, well blocked by Herath. That's STUMPS ON DAY 1.
Bouncer! Herath ducks in time to let that one go over him.

Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Sri Lanka inch closer to the 300 mark. Slower ball down leg, Dananjaya just helps it on it's way. De Kock couldn't collect it and the ball tickles away to the fence.
Dananjaya pushes this ball to covers.
Works this around the corner for a single. Useful runs these for the hosts.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Sharp turn down leg, Herath tries flicking the ball but misses.
New ball taken! Keshav Maharaj will continue to bowl!
Outside off, play and miss from Akila.
Pushed to the cover region by Herath. They pick up a single.

Akila rocks back and punches this through covers. Another run added.
Around off, well blocked.
Herath punches this ball to the off side. Picks up an easy run.
Dananjaya shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Slower ball on middle, Akila throws the kitchen sink at it but cannot connect. Gets hit on his back pad as the ball rolls to the off side.
Darts this on middle and off, Dananjaya blocks it off his back foot.
Sweeps this towards square leg and jogs to the other end.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Akila not holding back. Comes down the track and looks to clear the ground. Finds the fielder on the bounce at cow corner. One run taken.
Waits back and punches this ball to the mid off region to keep strike.
Cuts this through cover-point for a run.
Length ball around off, Herath goes for the cut but misses.
Flighted ball on off, Herath gets bat to ball.
Pushes this ball to the off side to give veteran the strike.
Flat ball on off, tapped to the off side.
Herath defends it from within the crease.
Rangana Herath is the last man to bat.

What a catch! Superman stuff. Markram has a lovely pair of hands and he holds onto this to add to his CV. Flighted ball around off, Lakmal drives it uppishly towards mid off. Markram at silly mid off flies to his left and takes a one-handed stunner. Lakmal is stunt. 08/109, that's the best figures for a visiting spinner on this ground. Grand style bowling from Maharaj!
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Slower ball on off, Lakmal gets forward and blocks it.
Suranga Lakmal, the skipper walks out to bat.

OUT! Maharaj strikes on the first ball to pick up his 7th wicket. What a day he is having. Bowls this full on leg, Perera goes for the swipe shot and connect it well. Unfortunately for him, he finds Ngidi at backward square leg.
Loopy ball outside off, well blocked.
Outside off, taps it in front of him.
Quicker one around off, pushed to the cover region.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Stays back and plays this ball to the off side.
Off breaker on off, cut towards point.
Aiden Markram in for another spell. Meanwhile, the new ball is dew after this over.
Perera has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Leans ahead and drives this ball to the off side.
Sharp turn pitched on middle, Perera goes for the cut but cannot make any contact.
Turns his bat to the leg side for nothing.
Loopy ball on off, driven to covers.
Punches this ball towards covers. Dot ball.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Length on off, blocked.
Short ball outside off, deliberately lofted over the slip region by Perera. It falls safe and the batsmen will get three runs for it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Length ball outside off, Perera guides this past the backward point fielder. The ball races to the boundary. The umpire signals four runs.
Akila drives this through the covers.
Tossed up ball on off, well blocked.
Defended off the front foot by Akila presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! A big shot was coming and Akila does just that. Charges to this tossed up ball and deposits to the long on fence. Boundary.
Comes in from over the wicket and lands this on middle and leg. Akila blocks it well.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Gets it through that region this time. Cut away by Perera for two more runs.
In the air.. just short. Short and wide from Ngidi. Perera square cuts and the ball falls just short of the backward point fielder.
Length around off, played back to the bowler.
Great ball. Yorks Perera, who does well to jam it out.
Outside off, played to point.
Gets behind the ball and is solid in his defense.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! First ball and he drives Maharaj. Overpitched ball outside off, Akila leans ahead and drives it in the gaps through covers. Boundary. 250 up for Sri Lanka.
Akila Dhananjaya is the new batsman.

OUT! That looked plumbed from the naked eye. Perhaps the umpire thought it took an inside edge. Maharaj serves this in line of the stumps. De Silva prods forward and looks to block it. Gets beaten and is wrapped on his pads. A strong appeal from the players but the umpire denies it. Faf straightaway takes it up. Replays show us three red lights. And that's the end of de Silva. Six wickets for Maharaj.
An LBW decision has been reviewed. Looks out or was there any inside edge?
Flat ball outside off, enough time for Perera to rock back and cut it to deep backward point. Gets a run for it.
Length ball outside off, Perera cuts it towards point to retain strike.
Outside off, left alone.
Back of a length ball around off, Perera waits back and punches it through covers. They come back for the second run.
Flicks this ball to the on side for nothing.
Kept low. Fuller ball on off, Perera does well to block it.
De Silva has worked it off his pads behind square. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! What a way to get off the mark. No fear in using his feet and gets four runs. Charges to this slow ball and lofts it over the bowler's head.
Driven towards the mid off region.
Dilruwan Perera strides out next.

OUT! Fifer for Keshav Maharaj! His fifth 5-wicket haul in Test and the hosts lose their keeper. Gives this air and lands this on middle and leg. Pitches on the rough patch and takes Dickwella by surprise. He goes for the sweep, the ball hits his glove and balloons over the keeper's head. Faf at slips moves to his right and takes a good catch. Maharaj becomes just the second South African spinner to take a 5-wicket haul at this venue.
Sharp turn. Slides in and takes an inside edge
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! Deft. Quicker one outside off, de Silva waited for it and cut it late through backward point for a boundary. All elegance in that.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Takes pace off this and serves this around off, Dickwella cuts it to the off side.
Fuller this time on leg, played to mid on.
Streaky! Dickwella will take it. Another short ball on off, Dickwella goes for the pull but gets an outside edge through the slip cordon. Has enough legs to touch the ropes.
Yorker outside off. Dickwella does well to get bat to it.
Short ball on off, de Silva pulls it towards mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Darts this on middle and leg. The ball spins and flicks the pads of de Silva. It goes fine towards fine leg for a brace.
Quicker this time, in line of the stumps, de Silva gets his bat down in time to get bat to it.
Goes onto his back foot and hits it to sweeper cover for a run.
Flat again outside off, Dickwella guides it to the backward point fielder.
Off spinner a tad short outside off, punched to the off side for one.
Niroshan Dickwella makes his way to the middle. Also, Aiden Markram in for another spell.

OUT! Gone! 139.1 kph and aimed at the stumps, fuller in length and it does the trick. Roshen plays all over the ball, it sneaks through his bat-pad, flicks the front pad and rattles the stumps. A fast bowler's delight to hear the sweet sound of furniture getting disturbed. Rabada has been everywhere today, taking diving catches in the field, making the ball talk and now taking wicket as well. More than that, he set Roshen Silva up really nicely with the short balls first and then slings in a full ball on the very last ball. Conventional tactics these!
Another short ball, Roshen sways away from the line and lets it be.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
On a length around off, blocked off the back foot.
Another yorker from Kagiso, Roshen digs it out from the bottom of the bat.
Yorker! Dug out to the off side.
FOUR! 3rd Test fifty for Dhananjaya de Silva. He gets to the landmark with a nice cut through cover-point. Elgar was generous as he bowled this one short and wide and de Silva made the most of it.
Comes down the track and pushes it to mid off.
Around off, pushed to covers for no run.
Comes down the track to play it to the on side but couldn't pierce the field.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Slower and a touch shorter, flicked to mid-wicket for a run. 50-run stand comes up between the two.
Short outside off, De Dilva pulls it down to the attacking short mid-wicket.
Full on off, driven down the ground straight to the fielder.
On a back of a length around off, pushed to covers for nothing.
Gets behind the line and keeps it out to the off side.
On a length around middle and off, pushed to mid-wicket. He looks better after some treatment now.
Goodness me, that must have hurt. Dhananjaya de Silva is on the ground with his hand on his shoulder. The physio is in the field. Meanwhile, the umpires call for the drinks.

A tad shorter around off, punched off the back foot. The batsmen take a single.

Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Some width on offer for Rohen and he creams the shot through cover-point. Runs coming thick and fast.
Defended off the front foot by Roshen presenting the full face of the bat.
A flighted ball turned into full toss by Roshen. He flicks it through square leg and a diving effort from the star fielder Rabada saves a couple for his team.
On the pads this time, Dhananjaya flicks it through square leg for a single.
Prodigious spin from fullish length, de Silva lets it be.
Wide outside off, cut to point.

FOUR! Streaky but runs. A back of a length ball around off, Silva pokes at it from his crease and the ball goes off the outside edge of the bat. It goes through the slip cordon and gully to the fence.
Roshen again leaves the ball outside his off stump.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Silva gets behind the line of the delivery and keeps it out.
Floated around off, pushed to point for a run.
Around middle and off, pushed to the leg side for nothing.
A tad shorter from Maharaj, Silva works it off the back foot. Another run taken.
On the pads, worked to the on side for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Soft hands from Silva saves him. A tossed up ball around off, Silva gets his bat in the line but again due to the spin, it takes the outside edge and runs to the right of Faf at first slip. A boundary results.
Gets behind the line of the ball and keeps it out. A maiden to start with.
Around off, punched to the off side.
Silva drives this through the covers.
On the pads, worked to the on side for nothing.
On a length around off, pushed to mid off by Silva.
A back of a length ball around off, defended off the back foot.
Drives this one to covers. End of a successful over for Maharaj.
Silva gets on the front foot and blocks it out.

During the wicket, Keshav Maharaj got a high five on his face! Aiden Markram wanted to give him a high five during the wicket celebrations but ended up slapping him on the eye. Laughs all around as South Africa celebrate.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

OUT! Impact straightaway. The man, Keshav Maharaj, produces prodigious spin on this occasion to take his 4th. What a start to the session for the visitors. A flighted ball on middle and off, Mathews plays the line off the front foot but the ball spins a little too much for his comfort. It takes the shoulder of his bat and goes straight into the hands of Du Plessis at first slip, who dives low to his right to take it. High fives all around for South Africa as Sri Lanka are losing the plot here.
Roshen Silva is the next batsman in.
On the pads, flicked to the on side. One run taken.
Starts with a flighted ball around off, driven to covers for nothing.

We're back for the third and final session of the day. The visitors will be hoping Keshav Maharaj along with other bowlers makes further inroads in this session. For the home team, Angelo Mathews and Dhananjaya de Silva need to stay out in the middle and bat out the day. Keshav Maharaj to start the proceedings with the ball. Let's go...
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

Sri Lanka will be unhappy especially with the loss of Mendis. He was going well but fell to a sweep shot. De Silva is looking confident and his partner, Mathews just got to a milestone. They will hope to bat another session. Join us in a while for the last session of the day.

Once again South Africa fight back into the game post the Lunch session. They have picked up three wickets and all have come from one bowler - Keshav Maharaj. He is getting the ball to turn and asking the batsmen questions. The pacers from the other end are trying their best but not getting their rewards.
Mathews chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump. TEA ON DAY 1!
Length ball outside off, play and a miss from Mathews.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! There it is, 5000 Test runs for Angelo Mathews. Cuts this back of a length ball through cover-point. No fielder there and the ball gets to the fence.
Punches this towards mid off and quickly gets to the other end. Faf has a shy but cannot hit the target.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Probably, the last over before Tea.
Bowls this slow on middle and leg, Mathews is solid in defense.
FOUR! Drags his length back, Mathews rocks back and slaps it through cover-point for an easy boundary. He now needs two more runs to get to 5000 Test runs.
Off break on off, this time Angelo goes back to defend it.
Gives this one air too, around off, Mathews leans ahead and blocks it.
Loopy ball on middle and leg, Mathews gets behind the ball and bunts it down.
Slower ball outside off, guided towards backward point for a run.
Length ball outside off, gets it off the inner half back to the bowler.
Angles this into Mathews in search of reverse swing. Mathews gives room and flicks it through mid-wicket for a brace. Gets off the mark.
Fuller ball on the fourth stump channel, superbly driven to covers.
Hops a tad and whips this away towards deep square leg to get to the other end.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Wide! Too high and the umpire outstretches his arms. Ngidi looks to dig this one short but bends his back way too much. De Silva does not offer a shot and de Kock collects the ball.
Ngidi just pulls out at the last moment before releasing the ball. Looks like his foot got stuck in an uneven surface on his run-up. The groundsmen are doing their work.
Length ball outside off, de Silva taps it in front of him to the off side.
Maharaj forces Mathews to go on the back foot to once again defend it. Good over from Keshav.
Maharaj gives this air around off, Mathews leans forward and defends it.
Quicker one on leg, Mathews goes on his back foot and turns his bat to the leg side.
Similar ball and Mathews sees it off.
Tossed up ball on middle, Mathews gets behind the ball and blocks it.
Flatter ball on middle and leg, flat-batted towards mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full in length, outside off, a straight bat is brought down in defense.
On a length, aiming the top of off stump, pushed back down the track from within the crease.
Full and angling back in, wristed away to short mid-wicket.
Just back of a length, closer to off this time, a mistimed punch from Mathews to the left of the bowler.
Outside off on a good length, Mathews leaves it alone.
Flighted ball outside off, well left by de Silva.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Slower ball on leg, defended by de Silva.

OUT! Maharaj gets his third and Sri Lanka lose another wicket. These two were playing the sweep very well and now Mendis falls to it. Loopy ball on middle and leg, Mendis gets low and goes for another sweep shot. He gets a top edge to it and the ball balloons towards mid-wicket. Rabada gets under the ball and takes it comfortably. Sri Lanka have lost three wickets post lunch for 60 runs. Also, Angelo Matthews is the new man in...
Nudges this towards the square leg umpire for a run.
FOUR! Short and wide and duly punished by de Silva. Stays in his crease and cuts it to the deep cover-point region for a boundary. 150 comes up for Sri Lanka.
FOUR! Ends the over with a boundary. Fullish ball by Rabada outside off, Mendis opens the bat face and guides it towards third man for a boundary.
Another fuller ball outside off. This time a more confident drive to the mid off fielder.
Pitches this one up around off, Mendis doesn't time his drive well. The ball rolls towards mid off.
Mendis stays in his crease and bunts this back of a length ball.
Short ball outside off, ducked under by Kusal.
The ball is down the leg side but Mendis still goes after it. Fails to make any contact.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up ball on middle, de Silva leans forward and defends it.
Takes a step forward and blocks it with ease.
Gets behind the ball and blocks it well.
Sweeps this in front of square leg for a single.
FOUR! Maharaj gives this air on middle, Mendis charges down the track and smacks it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Goes short again, De Silva ducks under it in time. De Kock completes the formalities.
Lands this on a good length on middle and leg, de Silva shows his bat sticker and defends it.
Bangs this one short again. De Silva sways away in time.
Works this around the corner for a run.
Dug in short around off, Mendis jumps and hits it back towards the bowler.
De Silva has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Quicker this time on off, played back by de Silva.
Bowls this slower on the fourth stump channel, de Silva taps it in front of him.
Darts this once again on the similar line, given back to the bowler.
Fuller one on middle and leg, hits it to mid on.
Quicker ball outside off, de Silva comes way down the track and blocks it with his pads. Appeal for an lbw, turned down.
Length ball around off, it swings away from Mendis. He looks to play at it but gets beaten.
A short delivery which has been pulled away to deep square leg. The batsmen have run through for a single.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
This one keeps a little low. Length ball in line of the stumps, de Silva gets behind the ball and sees it off.
Drives this towards mid off and hares to complete the run. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses.
Back of a length ball outside off, Mendis stays back and bunts it down.
Flighted ball on the leg stump, driven back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up ball on leg, flicked away to short mid-wicket.
Stifled appeal but going down leg. Slower ball on leg, it spins in and beats the defense of de Silva. Nothing from the umpire.
Loopy ball on leg, well blocked by de Silva.
Short and wide outside off, de Silva hops back and cuts it to the man at cover-point.

Drinks are on the field. South Africa have come back into the game with a couple of wickets courtesy Keshav Maharaj. Both the openers are back, meaning two new batsmen are in the middle. This next hour should be interesting.
Back of a length outside off, tapped away on the off side with an open face.
A short-arm pull from Dhananjaya. He swipes it across square on the leg side for a single.
Shaping back in on middle and leg, worked across the line to square leg for one.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Pounded in short, ducked and evaded.
Good length delivery from Rabada, Mendis blocks.
Kagiso Rabada returns to the attack.

Loud shout for a leg before, but the umpire turns it down! Maharaj was screaming for it. Dhananjaya dances a long way down the track in an attempt to block it. Wears it on the front pad and everyone goes up. Faf thinks of the review, but then decides against it. Wasn't too sure.
Full on the stumps, another block.
Dhananjaya plants his front foot forward and blocks it with the full face of the bat.
A hint of turn away, on off, defended.
FOUR! Too full from Maharaj, de Silva is down on his back knee and sweeps it with good timing through mid-wicket. Boundary results.
From around the wicket, spinning away, de Silva goes back and mistimes the punch to short cover.
A maiden over from the Steyn Gun. Hurls it in the zone of apprehension, Kusal Mendis covers the line and shoulders his arms.
Seaming away a touch around off, blocked down in front of point from within the crease.
Keeps it nice and tight. Hits the deck hard, around off, doesn't offer Mendis much room. He can only tap it down beside him on the off side.
Length delivery on the fourth stump line, Mendis covers the line and lets it be.
Full this time, outside off, blocked to covers again.
Keeps it close to off on a length, punched hard right at the cover fielder.
Another sweep, but this time just a single as it's placed to deep backward square leg.
Goes back and offers a firm punch straight to point.
Drifting in on middle and off and then straightening up with the spin, Mendis is forward to defend.
FOUR! A little too straight and too full in line, allows Mendis to play the slog sweep through mid-wicket. He earns consecutive boundaries with that. Nicely done.
FOUR! A little too full from Maharaj and Mendis puts it away with the sweep. Brings the broom out and places it through square leg for a boundary.
Tossed up. Drifting in at first and then turning away, Mendis is forward to block but gets beaten.

FOUR! Shot! Short of a length with some width offered outside off, de Silva latches onto it in a flash with a superb punch. Gets it in the gap at cover-point and beats the chasing fielder with ease. He's off the mark with that.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Short and outside off, Dhananjaya attempts to drag the pull on the leg side but only manages to get it towards mid-wicket off the inner half.
Goes a little fuller, swings it back in, de Silva positions himself perfectly behind the line and keeps it out.
On a length in line of the stumps, played towards mid on. Straight to the fielder.
Coming back in on a back of a length, de Silva rises on his toes and plays it back down the track.
Teasing stuff from Keshav Maharaj. He flights it up around off, Mendis is down to sweep but the ball goes under his bat and towards the keeper. Another wicket-maiden from Maharaj.
Spinning away from around off, pushed towards point. No run taken.
Fuller in length, blocked by Mendis.
Kusal Mendis to bat next.

OUT! Kagiso Rabada, take a bow, my good man! What an absolute beauty! The wicket truly belongs to fielder and not the bowler on this occasion. Maharaj tosses it up, Gunathilaka kneels down and brings out the sweep shot. Gets a top edge and the ball flies to deep mid-wicket. Rabada out in the deep covers a lot of ground to his left and dives forward to take a stunning catch. Both the openers are back in the hut now. Perfect chance for South Africa as two new batsmen are out in the middle.
Goes back and works it down in front of short leg.

Almost a bat-pad. Maharaj is getting some decent purchase off the deck. Behind a driving length, Gunathilaka is down the track to work it on the leg side. Beaten in the flight, the ball takes the gloves, then the pad and falls short of FSL.
Fraction too straight in line, easily clipped in front of square leg. One run to end the over.
Length delivery kicking off the surface a touch, blocked down with soft hands on the off side.
Full delivery on off, a hint of reverse, driven down the ground towards mid off. Dot ball.
Banged in short, on middle and leg, Danushka ducks and evades quickly.
Short of a length on off, blocked by standing tall and with a straight blade.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, arms are shouldered to this one.
Dale Steyn is back into the attack.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. A successful over from Keshav Maharaj, he'll be happy with this one. Wicket-maiden.
Slower through the air on the stumps, blocked again.
Full and straight on the stumps, blocked off the front foot.
Dhananjaya de Silva walks in at no.3.

OUT! Gone! South Africa finally have a wicket! Good stuff from Maharaj, a bit sloppy from Dimuth Karunaratne. Landed on leg, spinning down, the batsman looks to work it fine down the leg side but can only manage a faint edge behind. Quinton de Kock behind the stumps is sharp as a hawk as he moves to his right and collects it in his gloves. Partnership of 116 is broken. Can the Proteas pick up a quick wicket or two more here?
Uses the feet to get close to the pitch and mistimes the drive to mid off.
Turned with the spin to FSL.

FOUR! Edged and away! Short ball on middle and leg, the ball kicks off the deck. Gunathilaka takes the pull on but gets a top edge over the keeper's head. The ball crosses the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Comes ahead and drives the full delivery to mid off.
Keeps it on the stumps, blocked down on the leg side.
Full in length and angling in on middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for one.
A bit of reverse there for Lungi, Karunaratne uses the angle and works it straight to square leg.
Full and fired outside off, comes forward and blocks it in front of cover.

Tossed up in line of the stumps, Karunaratne brings out the reverse sweep and plays it through point. Not entirely off the middle though, as it popped off the splice and landed safely in the cover-point area. The batsmen want the second, but then decide against it as the throw comes in fast.
Flicks it away on the leg side with the wrists.
Punched off the back foot towards mid-wicket, where skipper Faf makes a good, quick stop.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Maharaj bowls this quicker through the air on the stumps, defended down on the leg side.
Spinning in on leg, Gunathilaka goes and works it just wide of leg gully. Single taken.
Angling in on middle and leg, on a length, worked to square leg with soft hands.
Another pull, down to fine leg. One more taken.
Dimuth swivels to this short ball and pulls it along the ground down to fine leg for one.
Good length delivery on off, it is blocked.
Maiden Test fifty for Danushka Gunathilaka! He too, like his partner, has played a fine knock so far. He flicks it off his pads on the leg side and takes a single to get to the milestone.
Fifty for Dimuth Karunaratne. His 16th in this format. Good length delivery outside off, Karunaratne punches it square through point and gets three. Lovely knock so far.
Reaches forward to the loopy delivery and pushes it towards mid on. Single to end the over.
Landed just behind a driving length, the batsman gets to the pitch and wrists it to mid on.
Flat, touch short and on leg, Karunaratne off the back foot clips this down towards fine leg. Gets two runs for doing so.
Uses the depth of the crease and nudges it on the leg side.
Comes forward and pushes it just wide of mid off for one. The 100-run stand is up with that.
Karunaratne works this full delivery towards mid-wicket and a rare fumble from Faf there allows the batsmen to take the single.
Full and straight from Ngidi, Danushka gets behind the line and blocks.
Length delivery on leg, defended.
Gunathilaka shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On middle and leg, moves inside the line and works it down towards fine leg for a single.
Hangs back inside the crease to the length ball and blocks it out.
Short of a good length on off, Karunaratne rises and taps it down in front of short third man.
Lungi Ngidi will bowl from the other end.
Well down leg again, swept straight to short fine leg.
FOUR! Poor line, needs to do better there. Maharaj bowls it around leg, Gunathilaka goes back and tickles it fine down the leg side. Beats the keeper and goes across the fence for a boundary.
Plays with the spin and tucks it just past short leg. Another dot.
Nice flight on this occasion. Full and straight from Maharaj, Danushka comes forward and blocks.
A bit slower through the air on the pads, the batsman goes back and works it past FSL.
Full delivery darted on the pads, Gunathilaka flicks it to the man at mid-wicket.

We are back for the second session. Sri Lanka are in prime position here, so the tourists will need an early wicket to begin things. Karunaratne and Gunathilaka to continue, while Keshav Maharaj will take the ball first up. A slip and a short leg in place. Let's go...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

The Sri Lankans will enjoy their lunch as both their openers remain unbeaten at the end of the first session. South Africa have found it hard to make much happen. Winning the toss, the hosts have used the conditions to their advantage and scored 93 runs. There were a few nervy moments, but otherwise Dimuth Karunaratne and Danushka Gunathilaka have done well. The surface isn't doing much to assist the bowlers, the seamers especially, so come the second session, Faf du Plessis will have to mix it up more and be innovative with his fields. The move to drop Tabraiz Shamsi for an extra pacer seems more strange now, given how even part-timer Aiden Markram has got the ball to spin appreciably. Let's see how it plays out further. Join us for the afternoon session soon.
Drifting in from around off, Karunaratne pushes it off the front foot to covers. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 1!
Outside off, pushed to the cover area for no run.
Loopy and fuller in length around off, the batsman has nothing to do with it.
Just behind a length, on off, guarded out safely.
A double in the long off region. Karunaratne hits it in that region and comes back on strike.
From around the wicket, Markram tosses it up outside off. Dimuth presses forward and pushes it to the covers. Elgar had to cover a lot of ground there, but still the batsmen did not pick up a run.
Works it away from inside the crease towards square leg for a run.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! The change in field brings about a different shot, but Karunaratne gets away with it. Tossed up on leg, he goes down and sweeps it fine down the leg side off the inner half. Across the fine leg fence and that's a boundary.
Full and straight, blocked.
Close. Quicker through the air on middle, Karunaratne brings his bat down to defend but it goes off the inner half on the leg side.
A leg gully in place now.
Flighted delivery around off, driven just wide of extra cover for a run.
Another one towards mid off. Another single to end the over.
A little too full from Markram, ends up bowling a full toss, driven to mid off for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Floated up there, Dimuth comes forward and works it just wide of mid on for one.
Seeing the extra bounce, Karunaratne goes back and keeps it out.
Landing on a driving length, Dimuth plays it off the front foot and into the ground.
On the stumps, blocked down in front of him with a straight blade.
Some extra bounce on the stumps, defended down in front of short leg.
Flicked with the spin through mid-wicket for a run.
Full and loopy outside off, driven wide of mid off for a single.
Some flight on this one, Gunathilaka defends it back down the track.
Full on the pads, worked away on the leg side.
Beaten! Lovely first over from Markram. Tossed up around off, it spins ever so slightly and beats the outside edge of the bat.
Full on off, pushed to covers. Dimuth takes the run on as Maharaj fires the throw. He misses and nobody is backing up. The batsmen steal another run.
Bit uppish but it's just short. Short and turning away with some bounce, Karunaratne goes back and checks his punch. It goes aerially towards the cover fielder but on the bounce.
Pushed away in front of covers off the back foot.
Full and slow, on the stumps, Karunaratne is forward to drive as he plays it back to the bowler.
Quicker through the air, on the stumps, Dimuth goes back and pushes it on the off side.
Aiden Markram on to bowl.
Full on middle and off, Karunaratne comes forward to defend but gets it off the leading edge a bit square on the off side. Single taken.
Brings the wrists into the play and plays another flick shot.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Another one flicked away on the leg side. No run taken.
Turning in from around off, Dimuth moves inside the line and works it away on the leg side.
Stays back and keeps it out off the back foot.
A good ball around off, it pitches and moves away. Gunathilaka leaves it alone on a length. Good leave from the opener.
Fuller on leg, driven to mid on for nothing.
Back of a length ball on off, Gunathilaka hops and keeps it down.
Gunathilaka shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Gets on the front foot and keeps it out.
Bumper! Left alone by Danushka.
Maharaj changes his angles and goes over the wicket. Gunathilaka works it to the on side for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Slower though the air this time on a similar line, Gunathilaka blocks it off the front foot.
Hangs back and keeps it out.
Shortish outside off, cut through point off the back foot.
Karunaratne fetches the flighted ball from outside off and gets it to the square leg region. Two runs taken.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Kagiso goes around the wicket and bowls a fullish ball. Danushka drives it to covers off the front foot.
Outside off, left alone.
Similar line and length from Rabada, Karunaratne gets an inside edge and the ball goes to fine leg. One run taken.
On a length outside off, kept out to the off side for nothing.
In line of the stumps, defended to the off side.
Kagiso Rabada is back.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but Gunathilaka still goes after it but misses.
Wrists it through the on side by Karunaratne. One run results.
Similar delivery from Keshav, defended by Karunaratne.
Lets the shortish ball spin in and gets it to the on side.
Swept through mid-wicket for a single.
Defends it off the front foot with a straight bat.
Full on off, driven to mid off for nothing.
Another block off the back foot by the batsman.
Karunaratne has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On the pads again, worked to the on side for a single.
In line of the stumps, pushed towards the bowler off the back foot.
On off, flicked through mid-wicket by Karunaratne. Three runs result.
Another short ball outside off, it spins in after pitching and Danushka gets it to on side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Shortish on middle and off, Karunaratne flicks to the on side for another easy run.
Shortish, punched off the back foot by Gunathilaka. One run results.
Tossed up on off, Karunaratne comes down the track and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Faster and flatter outside off, Karunaratne waits for the ball to spin in and works it to the on side.
On a length on middle, pushed towards Steyn who gets his hand on it and stops it.
On the pads this time, flicked off the back foot by Gunathilaka. The ball goes through square leg and a brace results.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller ball in line of the stumps, punched down the ground by Gunathilaka for nothing.
Angled across Gunathilaka who lets it be.
Angled across, Danushka blocks it off the front foot.
Tossed up delivery turned into a full toss, Danushka sweeps it through mid-wicket for a run. Not the start Maharaj would have hoped for.
A tad shorter and it spins down the leg side, Danushka flicks it to fine leg.
The batsman charges down the wicket. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Flatter outside off, kept out off the front foot.
Similar ball and similar shot from Gunathilaka this time. Another run.
Starts with a flighted ball outside off, Karunaratne comes down the track and drives it through long on for a single.
Spin time! Keshav Maharaj is into the attack.
Comes over the wicket for the last ball of the over. Gunathilaka leaves the ball outside off for the keeper.
Similar delivery from Dale, easily defended by Gunathilaka.
On off, blocked off the front foot.
FOUR! Nicely flicked. Steyn errs in line and Gunathilaka makes him pay. A back of a length ball outside leg, the batsman gets bat on ball and gets it fine to the fence. A boundary results.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Comes from 'round the wicket and Gunathilaka pushes it to the on side for nothing.
Change of ends for Dale Steyn.

Drinks! The Sri Lankan batsmen have tackled the first hour of play successfully. There were a few half chances but they survived. The visitors shouldn't be too disappointed either as they were in with a chance almost every other over.
On middle and leg, worked to the on side by Karunaratne.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Close to the off pole but easily left alone.
Hangs back and keeps it out off the back foot.

Another half chance goes abegging. A back of a length ball on the pads, Gunathilaka flicks it to square leg and sets off for a run. Maharaj scampers to his left and has a shy at the striker's end. He misses and a run results. He would have been gone had he hit the stumps. The 50-run stand comes up between the duo.
Around off, pushed down the track with the full face of the bat.
Around off, blocked off the back foot for nothing.
Ooh! Karunaratne fails to connect with the short ball as it hits him on his chest. These blows can be painful.
FOUR! Effortless this from Karunaratne. A back of a length ball from Steyn, the batsman just punches it nonchalantly off his back foot and through the cover-point region. A boundary results.
Driven aerially to mid on for nothing.
A touch short, blocked off the back foot by Karunaratne.
On the pads, worked to the on side for nothing.
Dale Steyn is back on.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. 10 off the over.

In the air... and safe again! How lucky both the left-handers have been this morning. None of the catches are finding the hands of the fielder. Another one which goes off the edge and lobs towards the point fielder but falls just short of Bavuma there.
FOUR! Confidence oozing in this shot. A lofted cover drive over the infield and into the fence from Gunathilaka.

Was there an inside edge? It didn't sound like it, perhaps there wasn't because the Proteas didn't really appeal. A length ball in line of the stumps, Danushka fails to defend the ball as it hits him on his pads.
Wide! An attempted bouncer which was well over head height. The umpire signals a wide.
Full outside off, driven to covers.
FOUR! Edge but safe. A length ball around off, Gunathilaka pokes at it from the foot. The ball takes a thick outside edge and runs through the gap between the slip cordon and gully.
Around off, pushed off  the front foot.
Defended off the front foot by Karunaratne presenting the full face of the bat.

Oh my word! The faintest of spikes on the Snicko saves him. It looked plumb had it not been for the confusion there. So what happens is, Rabada bowls a full ball on leg, Gunathilaka misses to play it as it sneaks under the bat to hit the pad. Rabada is convinced that it is going to hit the stumps but the umpire isn't. The skipper, Du Plessis, takes the review straightaway. The replays roll in. The ball goes off the bottom edge of the blade while taking its further journey which saves Gunathilaka. As a result, the visitors lose a review. One run added to the total.
We are going upstairs for an LBW decison. Faf takes the review. Gunathilaka is the man in question. He looks out. Or is he? Let's wait and see!
Outside off, left alone.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On the hips, on a back of a length, Danushka manages to keep it away from the short leg fielder.
This one didn't bounce as much. Another short ball from Kagiso, he angles it across the batsman. Gunathilaka gets his body and bat away from the line and lets it be.
Outside off, blocked.
Outside off, driven by Gunathilaka through mid off for a run.
Easy pickings this. A back of a length ball on the hips, clipped to square leg for a single.
Another fullish ball outside off, Karunaratne pushes it to mid off. No run taken.
Fullish around off, kept out with a straight bat.
On off, blocked off from the crease by the batsman.
Gunathilaka shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Wow! Zippy. Perfectly aimed bouncer by Kagiso. Gunathilaka does well to actually evade that by swaying away from the line.
On middle and off, flicked through square leg for a single.
Similar delivery and driven to mid on for nothing.
Fullish on off, pushed down the ground by Gunathilaka for a single.
Gunathilaka has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

A play and a miss. Nice testing channel from Ngidi keeping the batsman in check. A length ball outside off and entices Karunaratne to go after the widish delivery who does exactly that but misses. A promising over this from the third South African pacer.

Is this out? It looks out to the naked eye but no says the umpire. A length ball coming into Karunaratne who misses the leg side flick. The ball raps him on his pad but perhaps the angle would have taken it down the leg side. No review taken by Faf.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Around the wicket outside off, takes the edge off Karunaratne's blade but just like the previous time, it falls short of the slip fielder.
In line of the stumps from Ngidi, pushed through mid-wicket by Danushka. One run taken.
Full ball on off, defended down the track.
Lungi Ngidi is into the attack.
FOUR! Not the right line this time. Karunaratne clips it through mid-wicket nicely and finds the fence. A decent start for the opening pair and Sri Lanka.
And a full ball to follow up the short ball. Driven to mid on for nothing.
Bouncer! Karunaratne does well to evade it.
Fuller on middle and off, punched down the ground.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Around off, kept out off the front foot.
Tucked to mid-wicket to end an interesting over.
On off, pushed to covers.
And he finds the gap this time. On the pads again, Karunaratne clips it through mid-wicket region for three runs.
Around off and another edge that falls short. Karunaratne pushes at it and it takes the edge off the blade. The ball falls shot of the second slip fielder.
Similar delivery, it falls just short of Maharaj at short square leg. A wicket is around the corner it feels.
On the pads, clipped to square leg for a run.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Testing stuff from Rabada. Had there been a short leg in place, Karunaratne would've been walking back to the pavilion. Rabada bangs it in and makes him hop who gets a glove on it. The ball lobs in the air and falls in a safe area on the on side.
Half tracker once again, Karunaratne misses the pull and gets hit in the rib cage.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Five Wides! Too short this time and it evades a jumping de Kock as well. The ball goes to the fence behind the keeper and the umpire signals wide as well.

FOUR! Short and punished. Karunaratne is into the act now. It seems the Protea bowlers are looking to attack with the short bowling. However, the batsman was up to it this time with a pull. A boundary results through square leg.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

On a length outside off, Gunathilaka presents an angled bat and as a result, the ball takes the outer half of the bat. It goes through backward point and Bavuma hares after it to keep the batsmen down to two.
On middle and leg this time, pushed to the on side off the back foot by Danushka.
A back of a length ball on middle and off, kept out off the back foot.
Around off, blocked.

FOUR! Uppish but nicely timed. Gunathilaka gets his first boundary of the match with a beautiful cover drive. Steyn dishes this one on a fuller length outside off and gives the batsman a chance to free his arms. A boundary results.
Bouncer! Gunathilaka ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Fullish around off, pushed to mid on. Similar overs from the opening bowling pair for South Africa.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A touch fuller on off this time, Danushka comes forward and pushes at it with a straight bat. The ball races to long off but Maharaj cuts it down to three.
Angled across Gunathilaka by Rabada who lets it be.
The batsman tries flicking a ball that is down the leg side.
Rabada starts proceedings with a back of a length ball around off, Gunathilaka cuts it to point.
Kagiso Rabada to bowl from the other end.
Defended off the front foot again. Nice first over for both the teams.
Karunaratne chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Nice push. A length ball on off, Gunathilaka comes on the front foot and punches it. The ball evades the short mid off fielder and as a result, three runs are taken.
Coming on to the off stump this time, Gunathilaka happy to defend from his crease.
Similar channel from the fast bowler, ignored by the batsman again.
Steyn starts with a length ball outside off, left alone by Gunathilaka.

We are ready to begin. Danushka Gunathilaka and Dimuth Karunaratne will open the innings for Sri Lanka. Dale Steyn to kick things off with the new ball on this hot Colombo morning. Three slips and a gully in place for him. Here we go...

Faf du Plessis says they have worked on a few plans and they would try to implement them in this game. Mentions there are two changes - Theunis de Bruyn is in and there are three fast bowlers (The other change is Lungi Ngidi). States that on this wicket Sri Lanka will be more comfortable facing a second spin bowler, so wants to inject pace. Feels Test cricket takes a lot of application, unlike any other format, so they want to trust their defense more and get better results this time.

Suranga Lakmal says the wicket looks good and it's a good batting track, hence the decision. Informs there is one change as Akila Dananjaya comes in for Lakshan Sandakan. Reckons the cricket they played in Galle was their best and they would like to put in a similar performance this time out too.

Pitch Report - Russel Arnold doing the pitch report says it's a lot warmer here. Goes on to say that over the last couple of years, the surface has taken a lot of spin. Adds it's very dry, bare and has a lot of rough areas and also has a bit more pace and bounce compared to Galle. Continues saying there will be a lot of spin, so it will be a trial by spin again. Reckons the team winning the toss will bat first and they should put up a score around 270-300 and let the wicket do the rest.
Toss - Sri Lanka win the toss and choose to bat.

The Lankan bowling was equally handy as well. They ran through the Protea batsmen twice and managed to keep the combined total under 200, which almost embarrassed them, to say the least. This match should be another test for the visiting team and it won't be a surprise if they stage a comeback given their class and record in the longest format. The action starts in a while in the capital city, hang around!

Hello and welcome to the second and final Test match between Sri Lanka and South Africa at Sinhalese Sports Club, Colombo. After the debacle of the first Test, the visiting team will be looking to put some skill in their performance. Their batsmen especially need to get into the game and show some resistance. The home team, however, did everything right. Their batsmen used the home conditions to put up runs on the board, played both the spin and fast bowling effectively and essentially batted the opposition out of the match.
